NIGHTGLASS COURIER

A Place on the Round

The first market collection is ready. Aren can carry it to the landing—but can he let someone else finish the promise?

Two mornings later. Ninth round complete.

Give Kiva my morning.

Daro brought the packing stock up. His cart is below.

DARO
I would rather earn something on the way back.

KIVA
This set is Rusk’s. The buyer’s is still in the jig.

I thought I was taking it to Rusk.

KIVA
You are collecting it for me. We have not agreed the rest yet.

Rusk asked for the rear yard today. His long frame is in the front aisle.

DARO
You bring the box to the landing. I take the cart leg; her board comes back with you.

DARO
The cart cannot climb these steps. From that landing, the ramp goes round to his yard.

Aren collects. Daro may carr
end_text:
stairs.

DARO
Tell me the landing. I will tell you when I can be there.

East washhouse asked for first-bell collection next market day.

That is my morning round.

DARO
And I have not walked the collection door they marked.

We speak to the person handing goods over before either of us promises.

DARO
Tomorrow after your round. Meet here.

Later, in his own room.

How was the collection?

I only carried it halfway.

SERA
Did it arrive?

AREN
Yes.

Will you walk to the east washhouse with us after tomorrow’s round?

SERA
Yes. With the person handing the goods over.

End of Chapter 7
